newsitem.title: CHINA: China province ends soybean shipment curbs.
newsitem.headline: China province ends soybean shipment curbs.

text.p: China's northeastern province of Heilongjiang, the country's largest soybean producer, has relaxed restrictions on sales of unprocessed soybeans outside provincial borders, officials said on Friday.
"The policy was changed in December last year," a provincial government official said by telephone from Harbin, the provincial capital.
"Unprocessed soybeans may now leave the province."
Traders have said that the policy, in place for more than three years, had kept soybean prices artificially low in Heilongjiang and artificially high in other provinces.
"We wanted to adjust our industrial structure," a second provincial government official said.

"We were not making sufficient profits from selling value-added products. So, it's better to sell unprocessed soybeans." Heilongjiang's soybean output was estimated at 4.135 million tonnes in 1996, down slightly from 1995, provincial officials have said.
